title: The Relay
tagline: Twelve relay beacons before the station goes dark.
briefing: Command wants one order of 12 relay beacons. Every beacon is cut (3 ticks), assembled (4 ticks) and inspected (5 ticks), in that order.
You have 1,062 credits and 57 simulated ticks. Buy equipment, place it, publish the design, then run it: the Arcogine engine decides what happens.
A machine can only work as many beacons at once as its concurrency. Cheap lines queue; extra capacity costs credits. The score rewards spare ticks and spare credits.
Floor positions are only a schematic: where you put a machine never changes how it processes work.
hints: Find the slowest step for the whole order, not just one beacon: 12 beacons through a single assembler take 12 x 4 ticks.
Several inspectors can work in parallel. Adding capacity only helps at the step that is actually holding work back.
A twin assembler works two beacons at once. A flex cell can assemble or inspect, whichever is waiting.
